patterns.usage_note: Partial negation: it denies a conclusion the listener could reasonably have drawn rather than the fact itself, so it heads off a misunderstanding (特別つらいわけじゃない). わけがない denies possibility outright, and 〜とは限らない denies that a claim holds in every case, whereas this denies one specific inference. It attaches adnominally, with な after a na-adjective and normally という after a noun (学生というわけではない).

examples.ruby: この仕事[しごと]が特別[とくべつ]つらいわけじゃないが、朝[あさ]が早[はや]すぎる。
examples.english: It's not that this job is especially hard, but the mornings are brutal.

examples.ruby: 猫[ねこ]は魚[さかな]なら何[なん]でも好[す]きというわけではない。
examples.english: It's not as though cats like every kind of fish.

examples.ruby: 約束[やくそく]を忘[わす]れたわけじゃなく、言[い]い出[だ]せなかっただけだ。
examples.english: It's not that I forgot my promise, I just couldn't bring myself to mention it.

patterns.usage_note: The everyday plain negative: 未然形 plus ない on verbs (する becomes しない, 来る becomes こない), く plus ない on i-adjectives (高くない). ある is suppletive, its negative being simply ない. Polite speech normally uses 〜ません, with 〜ないです common but casual, and the ず／ぬ series is the stiff written counterpart of the same meaning.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]は今日[きょう]も部屋[へや]から出[で]てこない。
examples.english: My brother hasn't come out of his room today either.

examples.ruby: この件[けん]は誰[だれ]にも言[い]わないでほしいんだ。
examples.english: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone about this.

examples.ruby: 熱[ねつ]があるなら無理[むり]をしないほうがいいよ。
examples.english: If you have a fever, you'd better not push yourself.

patterns.usage_note: The classical negative auxiliary negates a verb on its 未然形: adverbial ず (何も言わず), prenominal ぬ (知らぬ人), colloquial ん (行かん), and the conditional ね, now mostly limited to 〜ねば and 〜ねばならない. The identical ね of そうですね is a separate entry, the sentence-final particle seeking agreement. する is irregular, giving せず and せねば, and ぬ and bare ず read as literary beside everyday ない, though 〜ずに is ordinary.

examples.ruby: 何[なん]の準備[じゅんび]もせずに本番[ほんばん]を迎[むか]えてしまった。
examples.english: I ended up going into the real thing with no preparation at all.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]がなぜ怒[おこ]ったのか、さっぱり分[わ]からん。
examples.english: I have no idea at all why he got angry.

examples.ruby: 一歩[いっぽ]も外[そと]に出[で]ぬまま冬[ふゆ]が終[お]わった。
examples.english: Winter ended without my once setting foot outdoors.
